title: Native Process Memory Reconciliation and Allocation Audit

root_cause_analysis.transient_vs_leak: Transient peak due to native C++ allocator retention, NOT a progressive memory leak.
evidence_against_leak: Python heap memory remained completely flat between 48.49 MB and 49.77 MB across all 240 requests.

In Block 4, native RSS peaked at 1092.86 MB during Normal shadow execution; immediately upon transitioning to the subsequent Disabled Block 4 run, native RSS dropped back down to 990.27 MB, proving prompt memory release.
In Block 5, Saturated condition memory stabilized at 1007.15 MB, well below the Block 4 peak.
root_cause_analysis.allocation_source: PyTorch LibTorch C++ tensor caching and OpenCV cv::Mat working buffers allocated during multi-thread feature matching under CPU thread competition.
root_cause_analysis.margin_verdict: Pre-registered margin of ±100.0 MB is strictly respected on an average basis (mean overhead +23.32 MB), but breached marginally on peak overhead (+102.51 MB, +2.51% over margin). Margin remains locked at ±100.0 MB without retrospective modification.
